originality.rationale: Trinas 2026 last-visits theorem covers fixed/o(sqrt(n)) targets, whereas the claimed k_n/sqrt(n)->nonzero c lies expressly in its open location regime. The closest public 2026-11-08 centered-interval theorem covers symmetric target intervals of radius c sqrt(n), not singleton points displaced by c sqrt(n), and yields a different swept-area constant (large-c slope 2 versus 1). Nontranslation-invariance of the elephant transition prevents equivalence by a spatial shift. Trinas–Valle supplies the LLT only. Fang 2025/2026 treats trained diffusive/critical first returns, and classical Brownian literature concerns a different process. Source full texts and actual search results were compared by implication, with residual priority risks noted.
residual_risks: The historical search is not exhaustive. An unlocated general last-visit theorem for arbitrary critical-scale target sets might imply the displaced-singleton formula despite not appearing in the inspected sources.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 primary paper explicitly lists target locations comparable to sqrt(n) as an open direction. A point displaced by this amount is the simplest natural critical-scale location test and cannot be reduced to a point at zero by translation. The result gives a sharp tail coefficient, full conditional position density, and structural geometry of the coefficient (evenness, strict monotonicity, large-displacement slope 1). The previous centered-interval geometry has slope 2 and hence the contrast is substantive. No broader theorem or exact elementary closed form is required for this well-motivated Brownian functional.
